Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Nair: hey, this is Priya, hi.
[00:10] Evan Holt: Evan here.
[00:12] Lina Gomez: Lina, hi.
[00:14] Diego Ramirez: Diego from Redwood, hi all.
[00:16] Maya Chen: awesome. high level we want to scope a POC that proves throughput and latency for Arkadia's clinical extraction pipeline and also test Spanish language coverage, is that right priya?
[00:30] Priya Nair: yes exactly. we have two main goals: one is throughput on batch ingest ~500 concurrent documents per minute for daytime loads, and two is p95 latency under 400 ms for single-document API calls for the UI. plus quality thresholds — entity extraction F1 > 0.88 for english and > 0.82 for spanish.
[00:55] Diego Ramirez: okay great, that's concrete. quick clarifying q — when you say 500 concurrent docs per minute, is that small docs (single paragraph) or longer discharge notes?
[01:05] Priya Nair: a mix — mostly mid-length discharge notes (~800 tokens) and some long referral letters up to 2,500 tokens. the Spanish set is generally shorter messages from clinicians 200-600 tokens.
[01:18] Maya Chen: got it. that helps a lot for model selection, batching heuristics, and KV cache behaviour — sorry K V cash in transcripts sometimes — the KV cache for conversational style isn't as relevant but prefix caching of repeated templates could help.
[01:36] Evan Holt: critical constraint from infra: we must keep PHI in our VPC. we prefer a private deployment but we can start hosted if the data is obfuscated for the benchmark. also need SOC2 documentation and KMS key wrapping for any dedicated nodes.
[01:53] Diego Ramirez: understood. we can run the benchmark using synthetic/obfuscated data against hosted endpoints first, then a dedicated VPC pilot with customer-managed KMS. Redwood has a private deployment option and the dedicated pool option — difference is Dedicated gives reserved capacity, Private includes your VPC and stricter network controls.
[02:12] Lina Gomez: timeline wise we want a 3-week pilot starting early June if possible — week 1 data ingestion & baseline, week 2 run model sweep and latency/throughput benchmarks, week 3 quality eval and handoff.
[02:25] Maya Chen: that fits our typical sprint. Diego, for the model sweep, what shortlist should we include for a health-focused open-model POC?
[02:34] Diego Ramirez: i'd propose three tiers: 1) small/fast: quantized 7B variants (we can try Llama2-7B Q4_x* style), 2) mid-size: 13B open models with better instruction-following, 3) larger 34B+ for quality compare. but because it's medical text we should include a medically fine-tuned open variant if available, or at least an instruction-tuned 13B. also consider multilingual-capable models like Mistral-Mega or a specialized multilingual 13B.
[03:03] Priya Nair: for spanish especially, we've seen good results with models fine-tuned on biomedical corpora — but if we can't get a medically fine-tuned open model, we're okay running a post-hoc re-ranker or a small adapter. quality is more important for spanish NER.
[03:18] Evan Holt: cost is a factor too — please include an estimate for hosted per-token cost vs dedicated reserved capacity cost for the 3-week pilot and for steady state 100k docs/day scenario.
[03:30] Maya Chen: yes we'll provide a cost sketch. Diego, make sure batching vs streaming tradeoffs are in the benchmark scripts.
[03:36] Diego Ramirez: Will do. i also want to capture success criteria formally: SLA p95 < 400ms for UI flows, sustained ingest throughput of 500 docs/min with average tokens per doc 800, quality thresholds Priya mentioned, and no PII leakage during benchmark — we'll use obfuscated payloads for hosted phase.
[03:58] Priya Nair: one more requirement: ability to pin a model version and fallback policy — if a larger model fails we'll fallback to a faster variant with graceful degradation.
[04:08] Diego Ramirez: Redwood supports model pinning and routing policies; we can configure automatic fallback to a quantized variant or to a smaller model. we'll include canary/rollback plans.
[04:18] Lina Gomez: about benchmark specifics — what metrics and tooling are you proposing?
[04:23] Diego Ramirez: benchmark matrix: latency distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, quality (entity F1, slot accuracy), and end-to-end UI latency. tooling: we'll provide a Jupyter-based runner + load generator (locust-like) and a results workbook.
[04:41] Priya Nair: and for quality evals — we'll need a held-out set of annotated notes; cannot be production PHI in early tests but we'll supply a de-identified set.
[04:50] Maya Chen: note on multilingual: some open models have degraded spanish tokenization causing performance regressions. Diego, add a tokenization/encoding check in the pre-benchmark steps.
[04:59] Diego Ramirez: yep. include tests for subword fragmentation and effective context window usage. also for long docs we should test KV cache evictions — if a 2,500 token note forces multiple passes, it affects latencies.
[05:12] Evan Holt: network: when you do the dedicated run inside our VPC we need to test egress patterns and ensure no outbound traffic to third parties. can you provide a sample network diagram?
[05:22] Maya Chen: we'll send a diagram and the private deployment checklist. action item captured.
[05:26] Priya Nair: thinking aloud: if we can't hit p95 < 400ms on long docs we may accept p95 < 1s but require p50 under 300ms for the UI. that's something we'll arbitrate during quality review.
[05:38] Diego Ramirez: okay we can tier the SLA by document class (short UI snippets vs long documents). in the benchmark we'll label document buckets so we can compute separate p95 targets.
[05:47] Lina Gomez: on model selection, can you list the exact open models you plan to include? we want to avoid proprietary models for compliance reasons.
[05:55] Diego Ramirez: sure, draft shortlist: "mosaic-ml/mpt-13b" (as a baseline mid-size), "meta/llama2-13b-q4" quantized variant for speed, "mistral-large-22b" if allowed for the heavier quality run, and a multilingual 13B like "open-multilingual/om-13b" (placeholder names), plus a medically-tuned community fork if available. we'll provide exact repo tags in the benchmark plan.
[06:20] Priya Nair: those names sound fine, but we need an option that has reasonably deterministic outputs for extraction tasks — models with more randomness complicate entity mapping. include temperature 0/0.2 experiments.
[06:33] Diego Ramirez: yes we'll run deterministic configs and sampling configs and capture effect on F1.
[06:37] Maya Chen: on observability — Redwood Console will give you token-level cost and latency, model-level dashboards, and traces. we'll set up an evaluation dashboard for your F1 scores and tie regression alerts to the prompt set.
[06:51] Evan Holt: for security: SOC2 attestation and KMS integration are musts; also need audit logs exported to our SIEM for the pilot. can you support pushing logs to our S3 with lifecycle rules?
[07:03] Diego Ramirez: yes, we can push audit logs to an S3 endpoint or to your SIEM via syslog depending on the setup. for private deployments logs can be retained per your policies.
[07:11] Priya Nair: about timelines — if we get the sample data by 6/4 and Redwood shares benchmark scripts by 6/2 we should be able to start the hosted synthetic baseline on 6/8 and the VPC dedicated run the following week.
[07:24] Maya Chen: sounds good. i'll coordinate scheduling and make sure the SE slot is reserved for the live run.
[07:30] Lina Gomez: pricing — we'll decide between hosted credits vs a short-term dedicated reservation. please include break-even points so finance can evaluate.
[07:39] Diego Ramirez: we'll include a cost model: pay-as-you-go hosted numbers, and reserved capacity amortized over the pilot plus steady state projection. include quantization benefits and batching effects.
[07:49] Priya Nair: one last question — can you support a light on-prem proof if our legal requires it later?
[07:55] Maya Chen: yes Redwood Private supports on-prem or VPC deployment. for initial POC we'll likely avoid full on-prem due to timeline.
[08:03] Evan Holt: agree. start hosted + dedicated pilot first.
[08:06] Maya Chen: quick recap of next steps: 1) Redwood to send benchmark template, network diagram, security docs; 2) Arkadia to deliver de-identified samples by 6/4; 3) Redwood SE to prepare runner and cost sketch by 6/5; 4) schedule live benchmark week of 6/8. any objections?
[08:25] Priya Nair: none.
[08:26] Lina Gomez: good.
[08:27] Evan Holt: good.
[08:28] Diego Ramirez: i'll share a short doc with the exact model repo tags and the runner README after the call.
[08:34] Maya Chen: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and share invites for the benchmark run.
[08:40] Priya Nair: thanks all.
[08:42] [meeting ends]
